about: Building traditions the engine draws (generic.trad_look): each with its look, kit parts, places and status; the shared kit of parts; the foundations every place gets. From the Traditions page, retired 13 October 2026.

traditions.look: Narrow brick fronts in dark reds and browns, a few plastered; steep gables with a hoist beam; white cornices on the oldest; newer brick lighter.
traditions.name: Dutch canal town

traditions.look: Limestone fronts in several tones, tall French windows with iron balconies, zinc mansards with dormers, chimney stacks with pots along the party walls.
traditions.name: Paris stone and zinc

traditions.look: Stone, Siena brick and warm plaster under low terracotta roofs with deep eaves; shutters at the windows; towers above the roofs.
traditions.name: Tuscan hill town

traditions.look: Painted timber boards in white, Falu red, ochre and yellow; steep tiled gables toward the harbour; white window frames; plastered blocks in the centre.
traditions.name: Norwegian wooden town
traditions.note: Bryggen at street level is not built: started on 2 October and not taken further. It waits behind the next map.

traditions.look: Stucco fronts in white, cream and pale colours, or London stock brick over a stucco ground floor; white sash windows; slate roofs; chimney stacks with pots on every party wall.
traditions.name: London terrace

traditions.look: Whitewashed cubes with softened edges and steps, flat roofs, blue domes on the chapels, blue and green doors and shutters, on cliffs above the sea.
traditions.name: Cycladic white

traditions.look: A plastered ground floor under dark timber upper floors, wooden balconies along each floor, wide eaves, dark tile or shingle roofs, on steep slopes by a lake.
traditions.name: Alpine chalet

traditions.look: Lime-washed walls, Roman tile roofs, wrought-iron window grilles, inner patios.
traditions.name: Andalusian white village

traditions.look: Pastel or azulejo-tiled fronts, Roman tile roofs, iron balconies, steep streets.
traditions.name: Portuguese tiles

traditions.look: Exposed timber frames over white or ochre infill, steep tile roofs with dormers, upper floors jutting over the street.
traditions.name: German half-timbered

traditions.look: Red brick Gothic, tall stepped gables to the street, black glazed tiles.
traditions.name: Hanseatic brick

traditions.look: Pastel stucco fronts with baroque gables, red tile roofs with dormers, cornices.
traditions.name: Central European baroque

traditions.look: Faded stucco in ochre, rose and red, terracotta roofs, funnel chimneys, doors onto the canals.
traditions.name: Venetian

traditions.look: Painted log houses with carved window frames; onion domes on the churches.
traditions.name: Russian wooden

traditions.look: White plaster and dark timber, upper floors jutting over the street, low tile roofs, minarets.
traditions.name: Balkan and Ottoman

traditions.look: Stone or whitewashed cottages, slate or thatch, chimneys at the gables.
traditions.name: British and Irish rural

traditions.look: Earth-red or blue-washed walls, flat roof terraces, inner courtyards, few windows to the street.
traditions.name: North African medina

traditions.look: Coral stone and white plaster, carved wooden window screens, wind towers.
traditions.name: Gulf and Hejaz

traditions.look: Adobe walls, domes and vaults, wind towers, tiled mosque domes.
traditions.name: Persian

traditions.look: Pale limestone, flat roofs with water tanks, arched windows.
traditions.name: Levantine stone

traditions.look: Smooth mud plaster, wooden beams jutting from the walls, flat roofs, buttressed towers.
traditions.name: Sahel earthen

traditions.look: White curved gables and thatch, or brightly painted fronts with flat roofs.
traditions.name: Cape Dutch and Bo-Kaap

traditions.look: Dark timber lattices, grey tile roofs with deep eaves, two low storeys.
traditions.name: Japanese wooden town

traditions.look: Grey brick walls round courtyards, curved grey tile roofs, red gates.
traditions.name: Chinese courtyard

traditions.look: Timber frames on stone bases, white walls, curved tile roofs.
traditions.name: Korean hanok

traditions.look: Pastel shophouse rows with covered five-foot ways, shuttered windows, tile roofs.
traditions.name: Southeast Asian shophouse

traditions.look: Timber houses raised on posts, steep roofs, wide verandas.
traditions.name: Southeast Asian timber

traditions.look: Pink or blue-washed walls, golden sandstone, carved overhanging balconies, flat roofs with domed pavilions.
traditions.name: Rajasthani

traditions.look: Whitewashed stone with walls leaning inward, flat roofs with dark parapets; carved brick and timber in the Kathmandu valley.
traditions.name: Himalayan

traditions.look: Clapboard in white and pale colours, asphalt shingles, front porches, gables.
traditions.name: North American wooden house

traditions.look: Brownstone stoops, brick walk-ups with fire escapes, flat roofs with water towers, heavy cornices.
traditions.name: North American downtown

traditions.look: Brightly painted stucco, wooden balconies, Roman tile roofs, courtyards.
traditions.name: Spanish colonial

traditions.look: Adobe or white sillar on Inca stone bases, terracotta roofs, blue balconies.
traditions.name: Andean adobe

traditions.look: Bright stucco or painted timber, verandas, louvred shutters, tin roofs.
traditions.name: Caribbean

traditions.look: Queenslanders raised on posts with verandas and corrugated iron; terraces with iron lace balconies.
traditions.name: Australian

traditions.look: Glass curtain walls, concrete, flat roofs; drawn from building tags in every tradition through its “modern” entries.
traditions.name: International modern

foundations.name: Traditions as data
foundations.what: Each tradition a short file: walls, roofs, windows and details by kind and age, with rules such as a Paris mansard or a canal gable

foundations.name: Mapped values first
foundations.what: What OpenStreetMap maps always wins; every guess is a real tag value, marked, with its reason in the tap panel

foundations.name: Each place’s own sun
foundations.what: The sun from each place’s latitude and clock

foundations.name: Real weather
foundations.what: The real hourly weather of each place at the same three moments

foundations.name: Terrain anywhere
foundations.what: Ground shape from open elevation tiles, about 30 m in Europe

foundations.name: Coasts and harbours
foundations.what: Mapped bays as sea; a coastline closed round the wrong side is dropped

foundations.name: Heights from neighbours
foundations.what: Where no height is mapped, the floors of mapped neighbours, never of towers or churches

foundations.name: Party walls
foundations.what: Walls shared with neighbours found from the footprints

foundations.name: Two image layers
foundations.what: Ground and buildings as separate images, each under the upload limit

foundations.name: Tradition by location
foundations.what: Choose a place’s tradition from where it is: a world map of tradition regions that blend at their edges

foundations.name: Local calibration
foundations.what: Shift a profile toward what neighbours have mapped: their colours, materials and roof shapes

foundations.name: Old town and new districts
